title: Welcome to your Pocket
body:
Droidian is a Linux desktop adapted for the Titan Pocket’s square screen and physical keyboard.

This tour explains the Pocket controls. Tap Next, or use A / L to move between pages. Use W / S to scroll longer pages.

You can reopen Pocket Tour from the app overview.

title: Give first setup a few minutes
body:
On the first boot, the phone expands storage and installs bundled packages before opening the desktop. Keep it powered and let setup finish before restarting.

Those packages are included in the image; first setup does not need internet access. Later boots should be quicker.

title: Home and quick settings
body:
Press Home to open the app overview. Tap an app to launch it or switch to it.

Press Fn + Home to open quick settings. Use the brightness and volume controls there.

The touchscreen remains available whenever an app is awkward to navigate with keys.

title: Your physical keyboard
body:
Fn + W / A / S / D gives up / left / down / right arrows.

Sym acts as Control. Back acts as Escape; what it does depends on the app.

Typing briefly pauses keyboard-surface input. Release physical keys before swiping: the pad does not report gestures while a key is held.

title: The keyboard is a scroll pad
body:
Press the red programmable key to switch between scroll and mouse modes.

In scroll mode, swipe on the keyboard surface to scroll.

Home is suppressed during a swipe and briefly afterward. Lift your finger and pause before pressing Home again.

title: Use it as a mouse
body:
In mouse mode, swipe across the keyboard to move the pointer.

Tap to left-click. Touch and hold to right-click.

To drag: tap once, then touch again and hold while moving.

Press the red programmable key to return to scroll mode.

title: Try the games
body:
Armagetron Advanced:
A / L — steer left / right
Space — brake
C — change camera
Back — game menu

Menus: W / S to move, A / L to adjust, Enter to select. Choose the Pocket preset if prompted.

Extreme Tux Racer includes tilt support. Long sessions and all control paths still need testing.

title: An experimental Linux phone
body:
Bluetooth does not work. Calls, SMS, mobile data, and emergency calling are untested. Cameras, microphones, GPS, NFC, suspend, Wi-Fi reconnect, and battery life need more testing.

System updates may overwrite Pocket adaptations. This is not yet a dependable everyday phone.

title: Make yourself at home
body:
This build starts the desktop unlocked and retains default Droidian accounts. You can change passwords and screen-lock settings yourself.

SSH is disabled. If you enable it, create fresh host keys and configure your own access.

Open the app overview with Home to explore. Tap Finish to close this tour.
